source_title: Ọjẹgbá rẹ Urhobo: Urhobo Grammar Basic Course (Urhobo Language Committee)

notation_system.description: Grammar course dedicates Chapter 1 (pages 8-15) to heteronyms and tone marks, defining the 4 canonical musical tones (M, R, D, ~).

tilde.meaning: Prolonged / drawn contour vowel (used in negative constructions and elisions)
tilde.example: Me reyõ; do (I will not take; thank you), ẽrha (palm oil shaft for fire)

orthographic_rules: Prolonged / negative vowels can be represented either by the tilde (~) or vowel doubling with a hyphen (e.g. 'Ọ diẹ ọyẽ' or 'Ọ diẹ ọye-e').
Homographs are systematically distinguished by tone: Oma (body) vs Óma (statute); Ẹvwé (goat) vs Ẹvwe (kola nut); Úko (back) vs Úkó (cup).
